relevance_rank_note: Measures ApoE isoform binding affinity to three LDL-receptor-family recycling receptors directly, by solid-phase apparent Kd and by surface plasmon resonance, so it tests B1 head-on for the VLDL receptor, LRP1 and the LDL receptor; the authors' conclusion is that the VLDL receptor and LRP do not discriminate between apoE isoforms, making the APOE4-versus-APOE3 contrast a null in every condition except weak lipid-free apoE4 binding to LRP.

description: Purified soluble VLDL receptor ligand-binding fragment was bound to apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 immobilised in microtiter wells, and the apparent Kd was indistinguishable between apoE4 and apoE3 (77 nM versus 59 nM), the authors concluding the VLDL receptor does not discriminate between isoforms.
quote: The apparent Kd values for the interaction of the VLDL receptor with immobilized apoE2, apoE3, and apoE4 are 86, 59, and 77 nM, respectively.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in VLDL receptor binding affinity, immobilised lipid-free apoE)
system: Cell-free solid-phase binding assay: microtiter wells coated with recombinant lipid-free human apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 at 4 ug/ml overnight at 4 degrees C, blocked with 3% BSA, then incubated 16 h at 4 degrees C with increasing concentrations of purified soluble human VLDL receptor fragment containing ligand-binding repeats 1-8 expressed in Cos-1 cells; bound receptor detected with anti-VLDL receptor antibody and alkaline-phosphatase-conjugated secondary; apparent Kd from the binding curve.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; the apparent Kd values are taken from the Results sentence quoted. Effect is recorded as qualitative because the authors print two Kd values but no ratio, difference or statistical comparison between apoE4 and apoE3, and the apoE4 value is numerically the tighter-binding direction (77 versus 59 nM is weaker binding for apoE4, since a higher Kd is weaker); the raw numbers are given here rather than converted. Effect detail: apparent Kd 59 nM for apoE3, 77 nM for apoE4, 86 nM for apoE2. No P value is printed for any isoform comparison. n = 2 from the Fig 1 legend statement that each data point is the average of duplicate determinations. The authors' own interpretation sentence, that the VLDL receptor and LRP do not discriminate between apoE isoforms, is what makes this a null; the human should confirm that treating a 59-versus-77 nM difference as a null is right to inherit from the authors rather than scoring it as a small apoE4-weaker effect.

description: Purified LRP was bound to apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 immobilised in microtiter wells, and the apparent Kd for apoE4 was indistinguishable from apoE3 (1.1 nM versus 1.7 nM), with the authors concluding LRP does not discriminate between apoE isoforms.
quote: The interaction of LRP with immobilized apoE was considerably stronger, with apparent Kd values of 1.6, 1.7, and 1.1 nM for the apoE2, apoE3, and apoE4 isoforms, respectively.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LRP binding affinity, immobilised lipid-free apoE)
system: Cell-free solid-phase binding assay: microtiter wells coated with recombinant lipid-free human apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 at 4 ug/ml overnight at 4 degrees C, blocked with 3% BSA, then incubated 16 h at 4 degrees C with increasing concentrations of purified LRP; bound receptor detected with anti-LRP antibody and alkaline-phosphatase-conjugated secondary; apparent Kd from the binding curve.
human_check: Decision 2026-11-23 (delegated to this session by the team leader): KEPT as against: true. Verified at source: 'The interaction of LRP with immobilized apoE was considerably stronger, with apparent Kd values of 1.6, 1.7, and 1.1 nM for the apoE2, apoE3, and apoE4 isoforms, respectively.' The apoE4 value is nominally lower (tighter) than apoE3, but there is NO statistical comparison, each point is the average of duplicate determinations (n=2), and the authors state twice that these receptors 'do not discriminate between apoE isoforms'. Recording an untested 1.7-vs-1.1 nM gap as support would attribute to the paper a claim it declines to make. A reviewer who prefers the printed direction can re-read it: both Kd values are in the description. No figure image was viewed; the apparent Kd values are read from the quoted Results sentence. Effect is qualitative because the authors print Kd values with no comparison statistic and no stated ratio. Effect detail: apparent Kd 1.7 nM for apoE3, 1.1 nM for apoE4, 1.6 nM for apoE2, so apoE4 is numerically the tighter binder by about 1.5-fold but is not reported as different. No P value is printed. n = 2 from the Fig 1 legend duplicate-determination statement. Recorded as against because the authors' stated conclusion is that LRP does not discriminate between apoE isoforms; the human should note that the raw direction (1.1 versus 1.7 nM) is nominally the H4 direction and decide whether that deserves a separate note in the submission.

description: Lipid-free apoE isoforms were injected over immobilised soluble VLDL receptor fragment on a BIAcore CM5 chip and equilibrium analysis gave Kd values that did not distinguish apoE4 from apoE3 (17 plus or minus 9 nM versus 25 plus or minus 10 nM).
quote: Equilibrium analysis of observed sensorgrams revealed a high-affinity interaction between the VLDL receptor and all apoE isoforms, with no distinction between them (Table 1).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in VLDL receptor binding affinity, lipid-free apoE in solution)
system: Cell-free surface plasmon resonance on a BIAcore 3000: purified soluble human VLDL receptor fragment with ligand-binding repeats 1-8 coupled to a CM5 sensor chip, with lipid-free recombinant human apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 injected as analyte at 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100 and 200 nM in HBS-P buffer pH 7.4, flow rate 10 ul/min for 3 min at 25 degrees C, dissociation into buffer, response corrected against a blank chip; Kd by equilibrium replot of Rmax against apoE concentration fitted to a single binding site.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; Kd values read from the Table 1 text rows. Effect detail: Table 1 Kd 25 plus or minus 10 nM for apoE3, 17 plus or minus 9 nM for apoE4, 20 plus or minus 5 nM for apoE2, overlapping error ranges, which is why this is qualitative with no printed comparison statistic. No P value is printed for any isoform pair. No replicate number is stated for the SPR experiments anywhere in the Table 1 legend, the Fig 2 legend or Experimental Procedures, so n is N/A + not_found_in_source; the plus or minus values are reported without saying what they are over. Lipid-free apoE in solution is the condition here, as distinct from the immobilised-apoE solid-phase rows.

description: In the same SPR experiment LRP bound no detectable lipid-free apoE2 or apoE3 but bound lipid-free apoE4 weakly, which the authors attribute to apoE4's tendency to aggregate rather than to isoform-specific receptor recognition.
quote: In contrast, LRP failed to recognize lipid-free apoE2 and apoE3 and bound weakly to lipid-free apoE4 in solution (Fig. 2D–F).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (weak detectable LRP binding where apoE3 gives none, lipid-free apoE in solution)
system: Cell-free surface plasmon resonance on a BIAcore 3000: purified LRP coupled to a CM5 sensor chip, with lipid-free recombinant human apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 injected as analyte at 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100 and 200 nM in HBS-P buffer pH 7.4, flow rate 10 ul/min for 3 min at 25 degrees C, response corrected against a blank chip; in parallel experiments disulfide-linked apoE oligomers were removed before injection.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; recorded from the quoted Results sentence and the Table 1 LRP row, which prints nb for apoE2 and apoE3 and the words weak binding for apoE4, with no Kd and therefore no numeric effect. This is the only direction in the paper that favours H4, and it is recorded as against: false for that reason, but it is weak: the authors state the apoE4 signal might result from the tendency of this isoform to aggregate, and that when disulfide-linked oligomers were removed from apoE2 and apoE3 no binding was detected at all, so the apoE4 signal may be an aggregation artefact rather than tighter receptor adhesion. No P value and no replicate count are printed. The human should decide whether a weak-binding-versus-no-binding comparison with no magnitude should count as a positive H4 finding at all.

description: In the same SPR series the LDL receptor bound none of the lipid-free apoE isoforms, so there was no apoE4-versus-apoE3 difference in LDL receptor binding under this condition.
quote: As expected, the LDL receptor did not bind lipid-free apoE isoforms in SPR experiments (data not shown).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change, no detectable LDL receptor binding by either isoform, lipid-free apoE in solution)
system: Cell-free surface plasmon resonance on a BIAcore 3000: purified LDL receptor coupled to a sensor chip with lipid-free recombinant human apoE2, apoE3 or apoE4 injected as analyte in HBS-P buffer pH 7.4 at 25 degrees C; Table 1 records nb, no binding detected, for all three isoforms.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. The supporting data are explicitly marked data not shown in the Results text, with only the Table 1 nb entries standing in for them, so this is a floor-level null with nothing measurable behind it; strength 3 is the weakest the checker allows at class 1, and the human may prefer to demote this row to class 3 with strength 4 or drop it. No numbers, no P value, no replicate count are printed. Lipid-free apoE in solution is the condition; the paper notes in its introduction that a soluble LDL receptor does bind immobilised apoE3 and apoE4 with high affinity, but that is a citation to Simmons et al., not a measurement made here, so it is not extracted.
